messages:
maria: Quick follow-up on continuous batching topology. Flat lanes gave better overall throughput but a few tenants hit high tail latencies due to KV-cache churn. Need to decide mitigation.

ashwin: where did you run it and what's the short repro?

maria: hosted staging (g4dn). load_test --tenants 60 --mix small:0.75,large:0.25 --dur 15m; batcher.topology=flat; slice_residency=4. Observed tokens/sec +10% but 2-4 tenants spiked >400ms and their kv-miss rose.

kevin: sounds like packing improved but slot residency fairness got worse. Two candidate approaches: per-tenant lane striping (micro-lanes) or residency leases (handoff lease).

jen: eviction churn would explain kv cold starts. Do we know the gap between consecutive schedules for affected tenants?

sam: we don't currently emit continuous residency gauges. Propose add metrics: residency_quanta_current, last_eviction_reason, kv_miss_rate_tenant. Also add accumulated_quanta to trace spans for correlation.

praveen: sketched a lease proto: lease {tenant_id, expiry_ms, allowed_quanta, renew_limit}. Lease prevents preemption until quota consumed or revoke. Bounded eviction storms but can hog.

ashwin: could scope leases to micro-lane to avoid global hogging. Alternatively soft boost: if tenant kv_hit_rate > th, give +N quanta for a short decay window. Less severe than hard lease.

kevin: we should also add per-lane circuit-breaker: max_quanta_per_window to prevent lane domination.

maria: proposal: try striping + soft boost first (lower-risk), keep lease option as fallback.

sam: experiment matrix suggestion: lanes={8,32}, residency={3,6}, soft_extra={1,2}. Run synthetic + real replay, capture p50/p95/p99, kv-miss, tokens/sec, per-tenant kv-warmth.

praveen: I'll harden lease proto and write RFC follow-up in case A fails.

maria: action items: I will open experiment PR; sam adds metrics/tracing; ashwin/kevin run matrix next week; praveen readies lease RFC. runtime-bot: CI presubmit passed for batcher-experiment branch.

jen: note: run a dedicated canary for Reserved/Dedicated infra to ensure predictability SLA isn't regressed.

maria: thanks all, posting PR link in this thread when ready. End.
